claims.statement: The Rust gateway is an optional executor on the model traffic path that makes no privacy or memory decisions of its own; every allow, block, and withhold verdict comes from PowerContext Core and the gateway only executes them in order.

The gateway README declares the gateway a working prototype verified end to end against a PowerContext Server branch (PR #2264), and it depends on the /v1/context/check contract and include_reuse from #2264.
The executor runs the phases in strict order: check before_send, then send admitted bytes only after an allow, then check before_release on the complete upstream response, then capture and release.
The binding returned by Core at before_send is reused as request_binding at before_release, so the release verdict is bound to the exact send-phase admission.

An allow verdict is accepted only if it has the expected schema, the expected phase, complete coverage, and a non-empty binding; any other allow is a malformed verdict that pauses the gate, so HTTP success alone is never treated as approval.

Each send attempt and the release verdict are checked against their valid_until deadline, and a deadline that has passed or cannot be parsed returns admission_expired without sending or releasing content, failing closed.
The fully rendered request body is measured against the input limit before the before_send check, and a body over the limit is blocked with request_payload_too_large without any Core check.
A release-phase block cancels the upstream request and returns a block outcome, so no upstream content is released to the client.

The ingress maps outcomes to client statuses: released passes through upstream status and content type, block returns 403, withhold returns 409, send_indeterminate returns 502, not_sent returns 502, admission_expired returns 409, and gate_paused returns 503.

Core unreachable (GateUnavailable) pauses model traffic by default and returns 503 gate_paused; the gateway passes the request through without memory only when PC_GATEWAY_DEGRADE is set to passthrough and the startup gate allows degradation.

Degradation is permitted only when Core's capabilities report enforcing=false at startup; a failed or invalid capabilities query leaves degradation disabled, and Core computes enforcing as mode equal to enforcing.
Blocked verdicts never degrade and malformed or other gate errors never degrade: degradation applies only to unreachable Core, and any other gate error pauses.
A degraded passthrough sends the pristine request without injected memory, records no capture, and marks the response with the x-pc-degraded header.

Core's check_context withholds every request with enforcement-not-configured when its inference protection mode is not enforcing, so a reachable non-enforcing Core answers checks with withhold rather than allow.

Retry is limited to attempts confirmed not sent; on NotSent the executor re-runs before_send to obtain a fresh admission before resending, and attempts are capped by PC_GATEWAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS with a default of 2.
The reqwest transport reports NotSent only for connect and request-builder failures; timeouts and any failure after the request may have reached the provider are Indeterminate.
An indeterminate send is never retried: a connection lost after handoff or a timeout returns send_indeterminate immediately, because the provider may already have billed the request.
Upstream responses are buffered up to a byte cap, and exceeding it returns withheld with response_buffer_limit_exceeded without releasing content or resending the request.
The Core-facing UDS client retries a request only when the failure happened before any response bytes arrived, which covers stale pooled connections, and never retries rejections or timeouts.

For a request in a conversation, the gateway prepares memory through Core's prepare contract with the last user message as the query, include_reuse enabled, and memory-only assembly; an empty or failed prepare injects nothing and never blocks the request.

Injected memory is placed verbatim in the last user message, and the exact UTF-8 byte range is declared in prepared_contexts; Core recomputes the digest of that range against the reuse binding and rejects any mismatch, so the gateway cannot alter injected bytes undetected.

Replay of prepared content happens only for requests with a conversation ID; the same message anchor reuses the exact prepared content and binding without another retrieval, and requests without a conversation prepare independently and inherit no injection.

The conversation ID comes from X-PowerContext-Conversation-ID first, then from Claude Code, OpenCode, or Codex session headers, and each source carries a distinct prefix so identifiers from different sources cannot collide.

When Core withholds with context-refresh-required, the gateway clears that conversation's replay entry and re-prepares once from the pristine request, so a stale reuse dependency is refreshed instead of being passed to the client.
Injection scope defaults to conversations only in a combined deployment and to off in a standalone deployment; on and off are explicit, and any unrecognized value disables injection.

When sedimentation is enabled, each terminal user turn is captured once after its response passes the release gate, using a deterministic source ID from scope, conversation, and pre-injection messages; a conflicting duplicate (409) is recorded as sediment_duplicate, and a failed capture never blocks the release.

The upstream request is always non-streaming; a streaming client receives the released or degraded response replayed as Responses SSE events only after the release gate has passed, and error statuses are returned as plain JSON.

In the combined deployment, selected by PC_GATEWAY_CORE_UDS, the gateway owns the public port, reverse-proxies non-gateway routes to Core over a Unix socket, and talks to Core over that socket; in the standalone deployment it talks to Core over HTTP and serves only /gateway/v1 and /healthz, returning 404 for other routes.

Core calls use the same GateClient operations in both deployment forms: check to /v1/context/check, prepare to /v1/context/prepare, and capture to /v1/sources/content, with the HTTP client using a 10-second request timeout and no redirects.

The model input limit is the minimum of the Core payload capacity, the 1 MiB Core parser ceiling, and PC_GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_BYTES, and if startup capabilities cannot be obtained or are incompatible the model routes stay paused until restart.
Middleware rejects model request bodies declared over the limit with 413 using Content-Length, applies a non-queuing concurrency limit that returns 503 when full, and exempts the health probe.

Upstream and Core credentials come only from server-side environment variables, and the header set forwarded in check payloads strips authorization, x-api-key, and cookie so provider credentials never enter Core payloads.
The evidence sink records body-free facts only, such as attempt counts, not-sent reasons, usage completeness, cache tokens, and time to first token, and never request or response bodies.

The Core client, upstream transport, and middleware chain are extension points: the executor depends only on the GateClient trait, the upstream path accepts only AdmittedSend values through the Transport trait, and new middleware is added to a chain composed in main.
